evidence: src/application/usecases/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts execute(): `if (request.lines.length === 0) { throw new Error('Order must contain at least one line'); }` is a domain invariant of the Order aggregate (domain layer).
src/application/usecases/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts execute(): `if (line.quantity <= 0) { throw new Error(`Invalid quantity for product ...`); }` is a domain rule for order lines (domain layer).
The domain entity is built directly with `new Order(orderId, request.lines)`, so these invariants are not enforced by the domain itself.
Orchestration that does fit the application role: productRepository.findAll(), stockManager.canReserveStock/reserveStock, orderRepository.save(order), mapToDto(order).
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Most of PlaceOrderUseCase.execute is application-layer orchestration. It loads products through repository ports, checks that each referenced product exists, asks the StockManager domain service whether stock can be reserved and then reserves it, saves the order and maps the result to a DTO. Those all fit the application role.

The problem is that execute also enforces two invariants of the Order aggregate: an order needs at least one line, and every line quantity must be positive. Those are domain business rules. They belong in the Order entity's constructor or factory, or in a domain value object for order lines. Keeping them in the use case means a new Order can be built anywhere else without these checks. That puts a domain-kind responsibility in an application file.

Generating the order ID inline with Date.now and Math.random is a smaller concern. Strictly speaking that is a technical detail that would usually sit behind an ID-generator port, but it is not clearly in the wrong layer on its own.

violations.message: execute() enforces Order aggregate invariants itself: an order needs at least one line (`request.lines.length === 0`) and each line quantity must be positive (`line.quantity <= 0`). These domain business rules belong in the Order entity or an OrderLine value object (domain layer), not in the application use case.
